meta.purpose: The two things about adjectives that LOD does not publish: which adjective is the opposite of which, and the suppletive forms of gutt.
meta.opposites: LOD carries no antonym field — the corpus has glosses and examples and nothing else. So every pair here is a judgement. What keeps it inside the corpus rule is that both members are named by their **LOD entry id**: not one word of Luxembourgish is written in this file, only a relation asserted between two entries that already exist. pipeline/build-adjectives.js refuses any id that is not a real adjective with a published comparative and superlative, and pipeline/test/adjectives.test.js checks the same.
meta.symmetry: A pair is written once and read both ways. An adjective may appear in several pairs — al is the opposite of jonk for a person and of nei for a thing, and both are true — so the game excludes every known opposite of a word from that word's wrong answers rather than assuming there is exactly one.
meta.irregular: gutt is the one adjective a learner cannot do without and the one LOD gives no table for: it models the suppletive forms as their own headwords (besser, am beschten) rather than as gutt's comparative. Linking them is this file's assertion; the forms themselves are LOD spellings, and a test requires both to be in content/lexicon.json.

GUTT2.note: LOD files these as their own headwords (BESSER1, BESCHT1) rather than as gutt's inflection table, so the link is asserted here. Both spellings are in content/lexicon.json.
